signin.kicker: Members only · ask at the counter
signin.title: What’ll it be?
signin.lead: Use the passkey on this device, or your username and password.
signin.leadSso: Use {name}, the passkey on this device, or your username and password.
signin.leadSsoOnly: Sign in with {name} — the same login you use elsewhere.
signin.passwordSet: Password saved. Sign in with it.

errors.inviteRequired: That address has not been invited. Pretty Please Print is invite-only — ask whoever owns the printer for a link.
errors.invalidToken: That link is no longer valid. Ask the printer owner for a fresh one.
errors.tokenExpired: That link expired. Ask the printer owner for another.
errors.suspended: That account has been suspended. Ask whoever owns the printer.
errors.emailNotVerified: Your sign-on provider has not confirmed your email address, so it cannot vouch for who you are here. Verify it there, then try again.
errors.emailNotFound: Your sign-on provider did not share an email address, so there is no way to tell who you are here.
errors.providerUnverified: Your sign-on provider’s answer could not be verified, so nobody was signed in. Try again; if it keeps happening, tell whoever owns the printer.
errors.other: That sign-in attempt did not go through.

form.refused: That username and password do not match. Try again.
form.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
form.passkeyRefused: That passkey was not accepted. Use your password instead.
form.inviteOnly: Pretty Please Print is invite-only — there is no sign-up. If you have not been invited yet, or you have forgotten your password, ask whoever owns the printer.
form.inviteOnlySso: Pretty Please Print is invite-only. If signing in tells you that you have not been invited, ask whoever owns the printer.

sso.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
sso.couldNotStart: Single sign-on could not be started. Try again, or ask whoever owns the printer.

account.passkeys: {count, plural, one {# passkey on this account} other {# passkeys on this account}}
account.docsHint: Every endpoint, and a console to call them from.

nudge.title: Tired of typing your password?
nudge.body: Save a passkey and this device signs you in with a fingerprint — nothing to remember, nothing to phish.

invite.leadLocal: Pick a name to go by, a username and a password, and you are in.
invite.leadSso: Sign in with {name} and you are in.
invite.ssoFor: This invitation is for {email}. Sign in there with that address and there is no password to choose here.

reauth.lead: You are about to change who can get in. A password or a passkey confirms it is you at the keyboard and not a browser somebody left open.
reauth.leadSso: You are about to change who can get in. Signing in with {name} again confirms it is you at the keyboard and not a browser somebody left open.
reauth.ssoNotConfirmed: Signing in again with {name} did not confirm it is you: it has to ask you to sign in there again, just now. Try again, or use a passkey or your password if you have one.

ssoOnly.title: No passwords here
ssoOnly.lead: This instance signs people in with {name} only, so there is no password to choose. Sign in with the address you were invited as.

passwordsOff.refused: Passwords are switched off on this instance, so there is none to set or reset.

sso.connected: Connected to {name}. Signing in there with the identity you connected opens this account.
sso.notConnected: Not connected. Signing in through {name} does not open the printer owner’s account until you connect it here — on purpose, so the provider cannot make itself the owner.
sso.connectNote: You will be asked to confirm it is you, and then to sign in at the provider as {email}.
sso.onlyWayIn: Passwords are off on this instance, so {name} is your only way in and cannot be disconnected here.

status.connected: {name} is connected. You can sign in through it from now on.
status.disconnected: {name} is disconnected. Signing in through it no longer opens this account.
status.failed: {name} could not be connected. Sign in there as {email}, with the address verified, and try again.
status.kept: Passwords are off, so {name} stays connected: it is your only way in.
status.unavailable: {name} could not be reached to connect it just now. Try again in a moment.

email.heading: Notifications by email
email.on: On. Whatever lands in your Activity panel is also sent to {email}.
email.off: Off. Notifications are in your Activity panel and nowhere else.

language.heading: Language
language.lead: The language of these pages and of the emails sent to you. “Follow my browser” uses the first language your browser asks for that is offered here; emails, with no browser to ask, then use this instance’s default.
language.refused: That language is not offered here, so nothing was changed.

adminSso.ownerNotConnected: Passwords are off and you have not connected {name}. Nobody can sign in as the printer owner. Turn local sign-in back on, connect {name} from your page, then turn it off again.

notification.storyMoved: {actor} moved “{title}” to {status, select, Requested {Requested} Accepted {Accepted} Printing {Printing} Done {Done} Delivery {Delivery} Declined {Declined} other {{status}}}.
notification.storyPriority: {actor} set “{title}” to {priority, select, low {low} medium {medium} high {high} other {{priority}}} priority.
notification.featurePriority: {actor} set “{title}” to {priority, select, low {low} medium {medium} high {high} other {{priority}}} priority.
notification.featureMoved: {actor} moved “{title}” to {status, select, Requested {Requested} Accepted {Accepted} InProgress {In progress} Shipped {Shipped} Done {Done} Declined {Declined} other {{status}}}.

shell.footer: You are getting this because someone at the office runs a 3D printer and uses Pretty Please Print to keep track of who asked for what. If none of that means anything to you, ignore this — nothing happens without the link above.
shell.fallback: Button not working? Paste this in:

invite.subject: {inviter} is offering to print things for you
invite.heading: You’ve been handed a 3D printer
invite.lead: {inviter} added you to Pretty Please Print. Drop an .stl or .3mf, say what you’re hoping for, and it goes up on the rail as a ticket you can follow.
invite.pill: ONE USE · EXPIRES IN {days, plural, one {# DAY} other {# DAYS}}

reset.subject: Set a new password
reset.heading: Set a new password
reset.lead: Whoever runs the printer reset your password. This link lets you pick a new one — it does not sign you in on its own.
reset.pill: ONE USE · EXPIRES IN {minutes, plural, one {# MINUTE} other {# MINUTES}}
reset.aside: Didn’t expect this? Have a word with them before you use it. Tired of typing a password? Save a passkey once you’re back in.

notification.subject: {ref}: {text}
notification.textWhy: You are getting this because email notifications are on for you in Pretty Please Print. Switch them off here: {url}
notification.aside: It is in your Activity panel too. Rather not get these by email? <link>Switch them off</link>.

test.subject: Test message from Pretty Please Print
test.text:
This is a test message, sent by {sender} from the Mail page.

If you are reading it, {passwords, select, on {invitations, password resets and notifications} other {invitations and notifications}} can reach people.
test.heading: Mail is getting through
test.lead: This is a test message, sent by {sender} from the Mail page. If you are reading it, {passwords, select, on {invitations, password resets and notifications} other {invitations and notifications}} can reach people.

adminMail.title: Mail
adminMail.intro: Invitations, {passwords, select, on {password resets, } other {}}and a copy of each notification for anyone who has not switched that off. Nothing here needs mail to work — without it you hand links over yourself and notifications stay in the Activity panel.
adminMail.noTransport: nothing — no SMTP_URL or RESEND_API_KEY is set
adminMail.badUrl: SMTP_URL is set but is not a URL
adminMail.fromEnv: The transport comes from <mono>.env.docker</mono> on the host (<mono>SMTP_URL</mono> or <mono>RESEND_API_KEY</mono>), not from this page — it includes a password. The sending address is <mono>MAIL_FROM</mono>, on the host as well; the name beside it is changed under Settings, unless <mono>MAIL_FROM</mono> already names one.
adminMail.previewsIntro: Each message as it leaves, with stand-in names and links that go nowhere. Every one also carries a plain-text version, for mail clients that will not show the other.
adminMail.subject: Subject

invitation.label: Invitation
invitation.when: Sent when you invite somebody, and when you resend it.

password-reset.label: Password reset
password-reset.when: Sent when you press “Forgotten password?” against somebody on the guest list.

notification.label: Notification
notification.when: Sent for everything that also lands in the Activity panel — a new request, a ticket moving, a comment — to people who have not switched it off.

test.label: Test message
test.when: Sent to you, from this page.

result.none: No mail transport is configured, so there is nowhere to send it.
result.refused: The mail server did not take it: {reason}
result.sent: Sent to {email}. If it does not arrive, check the spam folder before the settings.

auditSettings.cleared: (cleared a stored {value} that was not in force)

adminSettings.title: Settings
adminSettings.intro: The few things about this place you can change from here instead of the host’s environment file. A change applies to the next request — nobody has to restart anything.
adminSettings.lockedBy: Set by <mono>{name}</mono> on the host, which wins over this page. Remove it there to change it here.

passkeyRpName.label: Name shown when adding a passkey
passkeyRpName.help: What a phone, a password manager or a security key calls this place when somebody saves a passkey for it. Passkeys already saved keep the name they were saved with.

mailFromName.label: Name mail is sent from
mailFromName.help: Shown beside the address <mono>{address}</mono>, which stays with the mail settings on the host.
mailFromName.helpNoAddress: Shown beside the sending address, which stays with the mail settings on the host.
mailFromName.byDefaultNoName: The default: no name, the address alone, as MAIL_FROM on the host gives it.

defaultLocale.label: Language for anybody who has not chosen one
defaultLocale.help: For a visitor whose browser asks for none of the languages this app has, and for mail to anybody who has not picked one on their profile — invitations included. Everyone can still choose their own.

importSources.label: Importing from a link
importSources.option: Let people paste a {source} link instead of uploading a file
importSources.help: The server then fetches the model from that site itself, on the word of whoever pasted the link. It needs outbound HTTPS to it. Switching it on or off is on the audit trail.

adminSettings.reauthNote: If you signed in more than five minutes ago, you are asked to confirm it is you first.
adminSettings.allLocked: Everything here is set on the host.

result.saved: Saved. It applies from the next request.
result.unchanged: Nothing changed, so nothing was saved.
result.locked: {field} is set on the host, so it cannot be changed here. Nothing was saved.
result.invalid: {field} cannot be saved like that: use at most 64 characters, on one line, without " < > \ or invisible formatting characters. Nothing was saved.
result.invalidSources: That is not a site this app can import from. Nothing was saved.
result.invalidLocale: That is not a language this app has. Nothing was saved.
result.unknown: That form named a setting this page does not have. Nothing was saved.

env.title: Set on the host
env.intro: What this instance is running with, from <mono>.env.docker</mono>. Secrets are never shown — only whether something is set up.
env.methods: Username and password {local, select, on {on} other {off}}; single sign-on {oidc, select, on {on} other {off}}
env.mailTransport: {transport, select, smtp {set up, through SMTP} resend {set up, through Resend} other {not set up}}
env.howToChange: To change any of these, edit <mono>.env.docker</mono> on the host and recreate the stack.
